rituals.title: BIRTH CATCHER
rituals.mission: Catch the instant an unchosen thought begins.
rituals.play: Rest on one neutral point. When a thought appears by itself, catch only its first instant before following it.
rituals.twist: Classify only its form—word, image, memory, plan, sensation—then release.
rituals.win: You notice an arrival before it becomes a complete thought.
rituals.mind_bend: A spontaneous thought has a beginning you can catch, separating the arrival of mental content from the act of choosing it.

ONE RULE

TWIST

WIN

MIND BEND
A spontaneous thought has a beginning you can catch, separating the arrival of mental content from the act of choosing it.

rituals.title: DEATH CATCHER
rituals.mission: Catch the instant a thought stops being present.
rituals.play: Let one manageable thought remain until it naturally disappears. Mark the exact first beat of absence.
rituals.twist: Stay with the absence for one beat only.
rituals.win: You notice a thought ending as an event, not just another thought beginning.
rituals.mind_bend: Thoughts also have natural endings; disappearance can occur without replacement, argument, or a new thought taking over.

rituals.title: FIRST-WORD TRAP
rituals.mission: Let only word one enter the round.
rituals.play: Wait for inner speech. When the first word appears, hold that word for two beats and refuse to complete the sentence.
rituals.twist: If the arrival is an image, wait for its first caption word.
rituals.win: One word exists without automatically recruiting a sentence.
rituals.mind_bend: Inner speech becomes a chain only when one word recruits the next, so a sentence is built rather than delivered whole.

rituals.title: NO-SEQUEL
rituals.mission: Allow thought one but deny it a sequel.
rituals.rule: The first thought is permitted in full.
rituals.play: Let one thought finish. For the next five seconds, any explanation, defence, prediction or replay counts as a sequel and gets no continuation.
rituals.twist: A genuinely unrelated thought may enter.
rituals.win: The original thought ends without becoming a chain.
rituals.mind_bend: The first thought and its explanatory sequel are separate events; rumination begins in what gets added after the thought is already complete.

rituals.title: QUEUE MASTER
rituals.mission: Force multiple arrivals into a one-at-a-time queue.
rituals.rule: Only one item can occupy the front slot.
rituals.play: When several thoughts compete, imagine numbered tickets. Process only the lowest number for three beats; all others wait silently.
rituals.twist: After three beats, move the front ticket to the back without solving it.
rituals.win: Competition becomes an orderly sequence rather than a pile-up.
rituals.mind_bend: Mental overload can come from simultaneous competition, not sheer quantity; sequencing the arrivals changes the pressure without deleting any of them.

rituals.title: STACK POP
rituals.mission: Pop only the newest item from awareness.
rituals.play: When several thoughts are active, identify the one that arrived last. Let only that newest item fade or leave; do nothing to earlier items.
rituals.twist: Repeat once only if another clear newest item exists.
rituals.win: You experience mental load decreasing by last-in-first-out removal.
rituals.mind_bend: The newest mental item can be released while older material remains, showing that relief does not always require solving the oldest issue first.

rituals.title: LOOP COUNTER
rituals.mission: Count loops only when the same mental job repeats.
rituals.rule: Wording changes do not create a new loop.
rituals.play: Each time the mind revisits the issue, score +1 only if it adds no new fact, decision or action.
rituals.win: You can distinguish repetition from genuine thinking.
rituals.mind_bend: A repeated thought may feel productive while contributing nothing new; information gain, not mental motion, is what distinguishes thinking from looping.

rituals.title: TOPIC JUMP DETECTOR

rituals.win: A topic change becomes directly observable.
rituals.mind_bend: The thought stream contains actual subject-change boundaries, so what feels continuous is partly a rapid sequence of detectable mental cuts.

rituals.twist: If a link forms, label it BRIDGE and drop the bridge.
rituals.win: Two mental items coexist without becoming one narrative.
rituals.mind_bend: Two unrelated thoughts can occupy awareness together without needing a story between them; coexistence does not automatically create meaning.

rituals.play: Deliberately imagine a blue spoon for two seconds and release it. Then wait for any unchosen thought.
rituals.twist: Compare only the sense of initiation.
rituals.win: Chosen and spontaneous thought onset feel detectably different.

rituals.title: FORM SWITCH
rituals.mission: Translate the thought into another representational format.

rituals.win: The same content feels different when its format changes.
rituals.mind_bend: Meaning can survive a switch between words and imagery, showing that a thought’s format is not identical to what the thought is about.

rituals.win: You discover what the mind retained without active rehearsal.

rituals.win: The usual chain loses its uninterrupted continuity.

rituals.win: An explicit empty slot appears inside mental sequence.
rituals.mind_bend: Awareness can contain a deliberately unfilled slot, proving that the mind does not require every available moment to be occupied by content.

rituals.title: SPACED ECHO

rituals.twist: Do not rehearse either word during the final wait.
rituals.win: Spacing changes memory strength even though total repetitions are equal.
rituals.mind_bend: Identical material can leave different memory strength depending on spacing, exposing timing as part of encoding rather than a neutral container around it.

rituals.title: BINARY SEARCH
rituals.mission: Find a target by cutting the search space in half.
rituals.rule: Every guess must be the midpoint of the remaining range.
rituals.play: Pretend the target is 73 in the range 1-100. Walk through the midpoint decisions that a binary search would use until you reach 73.
rituals.twist: Never scan numbers one by one.
rituals.win: A large search space collapses through repeated halving.
rituals.mind_bend: Repeatedly halving an ordered range can locate a target without scanning each value, revealing how structure turns search from linear checking into rapid interval reduction.

rituals.title: BINARY BITS
rituals.mission: Turn 13 into four binary switches.
rituals.rule: Use place values 8-4-2-1 in that order.
rituals.play: Encode 13: switch ON the place values needed to total 13 and OFF the rest, producing the four-bit pattern.
rituals.twist: Decode your bit pattern back to the decimal number once.
rituals.win: One quantity becomes a positional on/off code and returns to the same value.
rituals.mind_bend: A decimal number can be rebuilt as selected 8-4-2-1 place values, revealing binary notation as a different decomposition of the identical quantity.

rituals.title: MAX-INFO QUESTION
rituals.mission: Ask the question that cuts uncertainty closest to half.
rituals.play: Imagine eight possible cards numbered 1–8. Compare asking 'Is it even?' with 'Is it greater than 7?' Decide which question would eliminate more possibilities regardless of the answer.
rituals.twist: Judge the split, not which answer you hope for.
rituals.win: A well-chosen question reduces uncertainty by dividing possibilities efficiently.
rituals.mind_bend: A yes-no question removes the most uncertainty when it divides possibilities as evenly as possible, making information gain a feature of the split—not of the answer you hope for.

rituals.title: REALITY PARTNER
rituals.mission: Use external verification for destabilizing uncertainty.
rituals.rule: Do not act on frightening interpretation alone.
rituals.play: Prepare one concrete question about what is happening and verify it with someone you trust or a clinician.
rituals.win: A real-world verification channel replaces solitary certainty loops.
rituals.mind_bend: A frightening interpretation that is hard to verify belongs in shared reality with another person, revealing external checking as a safety tool when solitary certainty is unreliable.
rituals.support_first: If you feel unsafe, disconnected from shared reality, unable to verify frightening experiences, at risk of harming yourself or someone else, or may be having a medical emergency, use real-world human/medical support rather than relying on an inward game.

rituals.title: HIDDEN-RULE INDUCTION

rituals.twist: The rule describes membership, not sequence order.
rituals.win: You infer the hidden classifier: accepted words contain at least one doubled consecutive letter.
rituals.mind_bend: Accepted and rejected examples can reveal a hidden classifier without any sequence to continue, showing rule induction as discovering membership structure from contrasts.

rituals.win: Memory of an experience can be disproportionately shaped by its peak and ending.
rituals.mind_bend: Whole-event memory may lean toward the most pleasant moment and the ending instead of averaging every ordinary minute, exposing selective compression in retrospective evaluation.

rituals.title: CARRY-OFF SUM

rituals.win: The altered-rule sum is 15, showing exactly how the no-carry system behaves.
rituals.mind_bend: Two-digit addition produces a different result when carrying is forbidden, revealing arithmetic output as the consequence of the chosen algorithm, not the digits alone.

rituals.title: WAIT WITH SOMEONE
rituals.mission: Use supervised delay.
rituals.rule: Nonurgent choices only — wait with someone only.
rituals.play: Stay alongside someone you trust for a defined period before acting on frightening or impulsive conclusions.
rituals.win: Time and company reduce pressure for immediate action.

rituals.title: TWO-SOURCE AGREEMENT
rituals.mission: Verify one fact twice outside your head.
rituals.rule: The two sources must be independent.
rituals.play: Choose one safe present detail—for example, current time or location. Check it on one external source, then confirm it with a second source or trusted person.
rituals.twist: If the sources disagree or you still feel unsafe, stop the game and seek human/professional support.
rituals.win: One reality anchor is supported by two independently checkable sources.
rituals.mind_bend: When two genuinely independent sources converge on the same present fact, agreement becomes a stronger safety check than repeated reporting from one information stream.
